title: Rhythms of Nature

standard_text: Natural rhythms and cycles: day and night, the seasons, phases of the Moon and tides; the water cycle; how plants, animals and people change with the seasons, including migration, hibernation and crop seasons (summary of NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 9).

key_big: Nature repeats its patterns again and again.
key_sub: Day and night, seasons and the water cycle.
body_html:
How to think about it

Nature has rhythms that repeat. Earth spins once in about 24 hours, giving day and night, and goes around the Sun once a year, giving the seasons. The Moon's shapes repeat about every 29 to 30 days. In the water cycle, water evaporates, condenses into clouds, falls as rain and collects in rivers and seas, again and again.

Living things follow these rhythms: migratory birds visit India in winter, frogs breed in the monsoon and some animals hibernate. Farmers sow kharif crops such as rice with the monsoon and rabi crops such as wheat in winter.

Example

After condensation comes…

clouds → rain

Answer: precipitation

Example

Wheat is a… crop

sown in winter

Answer: rabi crop

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Sun goes around Earth every day.
  • Mixing up evaporation and condensation.
  • Thinking rice is sown in winter.

faq.q: What are the steps of the water cycle?
faq.a: Evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection, repeating again and again.

faq.q: What are kharif and rabi crops?
faq.a: Kharif crops are sown with the monsoon (rice, maize, cotton); rabi crops are sown in winter (wheat, mustard, gram).
